MCP credentials on an unattended Mac

Prevent interactive MCP OAuth Keychain prompts on an unattended Mac.

About 2 min read · 1 sections

On this page
01 Existing gateway engines

Codex's default mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "auto" can read the macOS Keychain before falling back to a file. A Keychain authorization dialog can therefore hold an MCP operation open on an unattended execution host. Signing the executor gives it a stable identity, but does not remove locked-Keychain or per-item authorization requirements.

For a host whose operator chooses noninteractive MCP credential storage, set this top-level value in its native Codex config.toml:

mcp_oauth_credentials_store = "file"

This is Codex's supported OAuth file backend, not a timeout or a Keychain grant. It stores future MCP OAuth credentials in CODEX_HOME/.credentials.json. Protect that file and its directory with owner-only access. Bearer-token and stdio MCP configurations do not need to be removed. Provider subscription authentication is a separate setting and should not be changed for this fix.

See the official Codex configuration reference.

Existing gateway engines

The gateway copies client configuration into isolated executor homes. Shared generations preserve their existing snapshots, including across service restarts. Updating only the native configuration does not update those files.

  1. Resolve account-home configuration symlinks and update their owned target once. Preserve all unrelated settings and keep a private backup.
  2. Apply the same top-level setting to the host's existing executor snapshots, under state/desktop-generations/*/desktop-engine/config.toml, and the private state/desktop-engine/config.toml if present. Validate the parsed configuration before and after the edit and require owner-only permissions.
  3. Through each live engine's administrative connection, check config/read, call config/mcpServer/reload, and repeat mcpServerStatus/list. Keep replies in memory; report only the credential backend, server names, authentication statuses and tool counts.
  4. Reconnect existing desktop adapters normally when their work is settled. An adapter caches its startup settings and can otherwise supply an older credential-store preference when a new executor generation is created. Do not force a service restart to clear those clients.

File mode does not migrate OAuth tokens out of Keychain. An MCP that actually uses Keychain-only OAuth credentials may need a new login using the file backend. Never read a token into logs or delete the old entry as a diagnostic. Successful repeated inventories prove the checked live operations; they do not establish that every MCP is authenticated or exposes tools.

This is a machine configuration repair, so it needs no gateway release. Report any independent pending release adoption separately using gateway rollout --verify --json and its existing idle guards.
